New Forest's population decreased by around 700 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

New Forest's population decreased

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of New Forest fell by 0.4%, from around 176,500 in 2011 to around 175,800 in 2021.

This means New Forest was one of only two local authority areas in the South East to see its population decline. The regional population increased by 7.5%, while the population of England increased by 6.6%.

In 2021, New Forest was home to around 1.7 people per football pitch-sized piece of land. This area was among the lowest 30% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

The population of New Forest decreased by around 0.4%

An older New Forest

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of New Forest increased by four years, from 47 to 51 years of age.

This area had the joint second-highest average (median) age in the South East (alongside Isle of Wight and behind Rother) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by just under 4,300 (an increase of 19.9%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 6,700 (19.3% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 2.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

New Forest residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 158,500 New Forest residents said they were born in England. This represented 90.1% of the local population. The figure has decreased from around 159,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 90.6% of New Forest's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with just under 2,400 New Forest residents reporting this country of birth (1.4%). This figure was down from around 2,700 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.6% of the population of New Forest.

The number of New Forest residents born in Wales fell from just over 2,500 in 2011 (1.4% of the local population) to around 2,200 in 2021 (1.3%).

In 2021, 90.1% of New Forest residents reported their country of birth as England

Fall in employment

New Forest saw the South East's third-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed (from 54.9% in 2011 to 51.8% in 2021).

Across the region, only West Oxfordshire (from 65.1% to 61.7%) and West Berkshire (from 65.0% to 61.7%) saw a greater decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in New Forest decreased by 3.2 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 12.9% of New Forest residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 12.2% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in eight people (11.9%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 14.2% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 53.0% to 54.2%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week in New Forest (0.7 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (0.5 percentage points, from 10.4% to 11.0%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in New Forest increased by 0.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in New Forest

In 2021, 5.0% of New Forest residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 8.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.5% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.2% in 2011. The proportion of New Forest residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.3% to 2.5%.

This area had the region’s joint second highest proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (alongside Rother, Mole Valley and Adur). Across the region, only Lewes, with 5.4%, had a higher proportion.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in New Forest decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Religion in New Forest

In 2021, 40.7% of New Forest residents reported having "No religion", up from 25.7% in 2011. The rise of 15.0 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in New Forest. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 51.6% of people in New Forest described themselves as Christian (down from 65.2%), while 6.1% did not state their religion (down from 7.8% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 40.7% of usual residents in New Forest reported having "No religion"

National identity in New Forest

In 2021, 3.1% of New Forest residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.6% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.1% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.5% in 2011. The percentage of residents in New Forest that identified as "British only" increased from 15.4% to 57.5%.

This area had the region’s joint third lowest percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK (alongside Gosport). Across the region, only Havant (2.7%) and Fareham (2.8%) had a lower percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in New Forest increased by 0.5 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

Of New Forest households, 18.4% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in six households (16.4%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 17.7% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 6.2% to 6.7%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children in New Forest (1.5 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.4 percentage points, from 18.7% to 17.4%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in New Forest decreased by 1.5 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of New Forest residents aged 16 years and over, 26.9% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 24.5% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (52.4%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 54.6% in 2011. The percentage of adults in New Forest that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.7% to 10.4%.

This area had the country's joint lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership (alongside Hambleton). North Norfolk had England's next-lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership (27.2%), while Lambeth had the country's highest percentage (62.2%).

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in New Forest increased by 2.4 percentage points

Change in housing in New Forest

Of New Forest households, 74.2% owned their home in 2021, down from 75.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in seven households (14.3%) rented privately, compared with 12.1% in 2011. The percentage of New Forest households that lived in a socially rented property decreased from 11.0% to 10.8%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater across the South East (2.0 percentage points, from 67.6% to 65.7%) than in New Forest (0.8 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in New Forest decreased by 0.8 percentage points

Disability in New Forest

In 2021, 6.1% of New Forest residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.2%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.5% in 2011. The proportion of New Forest residents who were not disabled decreased from 83.8% to 83.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%) than in New Forest (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in New Forest decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Health in New Forest

In 2021, 50.5% of New Forest residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 48.3% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.3% to 34.3%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of New Forest residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.8% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.2% to 3.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in New Forest increased by 2.2 percentage points

Ethnic groups in New Forest

In 2021, 1.2% of New Forest residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 0.9% in 2011. The 0.3 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 96.8% of people in New Forest identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.6% in 2011), while 1.3% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 0.9% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.2% in 2011 to 0.4% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 1.2% of usual residents in New Forest identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category
